_comment: An EXAMPLE EndpointRoutingSnapshot.  The portal's registry writes this
shape; the gateway reads it and nothing else.  Every value here is
synthetic -- the addresses, the secret files and the model ids are
placeholders, and the users are the four platform accounts the brief
names, shown once each so the three ACL kinds are all visible.
It is loaded with `--routing-snapshot PATH`.  Without that flag the
gateway has exactly the single upstream it had before this file existed.
The file must be a regular file, owned by root or by the gateway's own
user, and not group- or other-writable; anything else is refused and
reported in status.json under routing.error.  There is no signature here:
the trust model is 'read-only and trusted', and the sha256 of what was
actually loaded is published in the status document so an operator can
tell whether what is in force is what they approved.
`secret_ref` names a file and a variable inside it -- never a value.
An inline secret would put a credential in a file the registry writes.
`transport` is `http` (an IP literal, loopback unless the operator
allowlisted the address on the command line) or `unix` (an absolute
socket path).  There is no third option: no DNS, no file://, no scheme

endpoints.note: the house model; the only one every platform user may call
{{LAB_USER}}'s own; nobody else sees it, including in /v1/models
shared with one named user and with one trusted uid; both forms are exact
